title: Wrapping up the project
objective: Connect buttons and the keyboard to the same function, make accessible controls, and organize code with init/render/update
story: Your project is almost ready, captain! But when your friend opens it on a phone, there's no keyboard and the screen is small. Today we're making your project useful **for everyone**: touch controls, small screens and **accessibility**.

sections.title: Phones have no keyboard
Small screens and matchMedia
Accessibility: everyone can use it
sections.body:
Some users can't see the screen and use a **screen reader**; some can't use a mouse and move around with only the keyboard. A few habits make a big difference:

- Use `<button>`, not `<div>`, for things that get clicked: a button can be selected with Tab and works with Enter and Space on its own.
- Give a button that is only an icon an `aria-label`: `btn.setAttribute("aria-label", "Go left")`. The screen reader reads this instead of ◀.
- On the button of a menu that opens and closes, `aria-expanded` should be `"true"` or `"false"`.
- For messages that change by themselves (`Correct!`, `Saved`), add `aria-live="polite"` to the box; the screen reader reads the change.
- `element.focus()` moves the keyboard focus to an element. When a menu closes, give the focus back to the button that opened it.

tasks.title: One function, two ways
tasks.prompt:
Write the `move(dx)` function and connect it to both the buttons and the arrow keys:

- `move(dx)`: change `x` by `dx`; `x` must stay between 0 and 100. Write `Position: 60` into `#pos`.
- When the `#left` and `#right` buttons are clicked, call `move(-10)` / `move(10)`.
- The `ArrowLeft` and `ArrowRight` keys should call the **same** function.
tasks.html: Position: 50

tasks.title: Labels and focus
tasks.prompt:
The ▶ and ■ buttons are only icons; a screen reader can't tell what they do. Fix it:

- Give `#play` the `aria-label` `Start` and `#stop` the label `Stop` (`setAttribute`).
- When `#play` is clicked, `#status` should say `Running` and the keyboard focus should move to `#stop` (`focus()`).
- When `#stop` is clicked, `#status` should say `Stopped` and the focus should go back to `#play`.

tasks.title: init, update, render
tasks.prompt:
Write the fuel gauge with the three-part layout (`state` is ready):

- `update(action)`: if `"burn"` comes in, the fuel goes down by 20 (not below 0); if `"refill"` comes in, it becomes 100. It must not touch the screen.
- `render()`: write `Fuel: 80` into `#fuel`; if the fuel is 20 or less, add the `low` class to `#fuel`, otherwise remove it.
- `init()`: connect the `#burn` and `#refill` buttons (on click: `update`, then `render`) and call `render` once.
hints: classList.toggle("low", state.fuel <= 20) adds or removes the class depending on the condition.
Don't forget to call render(); at the end of init.

challenge.title: A keyboard menu
challenge.prompt:
Let users move between the menu buttons with the arrow keys:

- Inside `#menu`, `ArrowDown` moves the focus to the next button and `ArrowUp` to the previous one (`focus()`).
- Wrap around at the ends: going down from the last one goes to the first, and going up from the first goes to the last.
- When a button is clicked, write `Selected: Settings` into `#info`.

Hint: `e.target` gives the button the event came from, and `items.indexOf(e.target)` gives its position.
hints: To wrap around, use the remainder: (index + count) % count

project_task.title: Mobile controls
project_task.prompt:
Let's make it playable on a phone too! In the old code, movement works only with the keyboard, and the logic is buried inside the event. Tidy it up:

- `moveShip(dx)`: change `ship.x`; the ship must not leave the canvas (between 0 and `canvas.width - SHIP_SIZE`); then call `draw()`.
- The keyboard (`ArrowLeft` / `ArrowRight`) and the on-screen `#btn-left` / `#btn-right` buttons should call the **same** `moveShip` (step: `STEP`).
- Give the icon buttons an `aria-label`: `Left` and `Right`.
project_task.html: Star Hunter
hints: function moveShip(dx) { ship.x = Math.min(maxX, Math.max(0, ship.x + dx)); draw(); }
Change the old keydown code so it calls moveShip(-STEP) / moveShip(STEP).
